x-interview.ask: Who is the book for — which reader age band?

style.description: Short human-readable illustration style label, e.g. 'soft watercolor, pastel palette'. Used in prose (image_prompts mention it) and as a quick summary; the paid scripts inject 'style_guide' (required) into every API call, not this field.

x-interview.ask: What illustration style? E.g. soft watercolor (default), bold flat cartoon, colored-pencil, paper-cutout collage — or describe your own.

style_guide.description: REQUIRED structured style guide. The render and stylesheet scripts assemble a single deterministic style block from these fields (in fixed order: medium → palette → line → lighting → mood) and inject it byte-identically into every API call. This locks book-wide visual consistency — each page is a separate stateless API call, and having the exact same verbatim block in every prompt is the documented consistency mechanism (per Google's Book_illustration workflow). Both paid scripts refuse to run when this object is missing or empty. At least one field must be set.

medium.description: Rendering medium and technique, e.g. 'soft watercolor with pen-and-ink outline'.

palette.description: 3–5 named or hex color swatches that define the book's palette, e.g. ['warm cream #F5E9D4', 'sage green #8FAF85', 'dusty coral #E8917A']. These are injected verbatim — the more specific, the better the cross-page consistency.

line.description: Line-work description, e.g. 'thin sepia ink, even weight, rounded corners'.

lighting.description: Lighting direction, quality, and color temperature, e.g. 'golden-hour side-light, soft warm shadows, no harsh edges'.

mood.description: Overall mood and rendering vocabulary, e.g. 'cozy, gentle, storybook calm, slightly naive brushwork'.

cast.description: Explicit unified cast: every recurring visual subject in the book — characters, recognisable objects, and named places. ONE entry per REAL subject. Drives Stage 2 (one reference sheet per eligible entry) and Stage 3 (per-page reference selection). Never rely on auto-extraction from prose.

name.description: Name exactly as written in image_prompts and pages[].cast.

kind.description: What this entry is. 'character' (default): person or creature — gets a style sheet; the outfit lock applies; eligible to be a page hero (first character-kind entry in pages[].cast additionally contributes its reference photo). 'object': recurring prop, vehicle, or item — gets a reference sheet with multi-angle/detail-close-up prompt. 'location': a named place — when ref_image is set, the real-place photo is the render reference and NO sheet is generated (the photo is sent at render time as lowest-priority reference, PER-38 flow); without ref_image a location reference sheet is generated from 'appearance' (fictional recurring place).

appearance.description: Concrete visual description. character: species, age, hair, ONE specific outfit/clothing, colours, distinguishing features — the outfit named here becomes the character's canonical outfit locked into the style sheet and worn unchanged on every page (name exactly one outfit; more specific = more consistent). object: shape, size, colours, materials, distinguishing details. location: terrain/architecture, vegetation, landmarks, atmosphere — feeds the sheet prompt when no ref_image is given.

ref_image.description: Optional reference photo(s). kind=character: a single absolute path or an array of paths; EVERY image must show ONLY this character (single-person images only — crop multi-person photos with scripts/crop_character.py first; never reference the original multi-person photo); used for face and hair likeness only — clothing/outfit always comes from 'appearance', not these photos; capped at 5 (Gemini 3 Pro Image character-lane limit). kind=object: photo(s) of the object (single path or array); shape/colour/detail reference; capped at 5. kind=location: ONE real-place photo as a plain string (loc-{slug}.jpg produced by fetch_location.py); when set, no style sheet is generated — the photo is sent at render time; use an array only for multiple angles (cap 5 still applies).

style_sheet.description: Path to this entry's generated reference sheet PNG (filled in by make_style_sheet.py). Never set for kind=location entries that carry a ref_image (those use the photo directly).

source_url.description: Optional provenance for a downloaded reference photo (prefer the Wikimedia Commons file page — it carries license and attribution). Relevant for kind=location entries whose ref_image was produced by fetch_location.py.

text_mode.description: How page text is rendered. 'native' (default): ask the image model to render the story text directly into the illustration (output goes to page-NN-native.png). 'overlay': generate image with a text-safe zone, then Pillow-composite text via overlay_text.py. 'long': each body page becomes two physical pages — (1) full-bleed art with no text (pages/page-NN-long.png), (2) a separate text-only page with the story text on a centered, feathered semi-transparent panel over ONE shared model-generated background reused book-wide (pages/text-bg-long.png; designed with a reserved low-detail central text area). Cover (page 1) stays a single combined overlay-style page. Cost = N art calls + 1 shared-background call; a page with 'text_background_prompt' gets its own dedicated background instead (+1 call for that page). render_book.py's --text-mode flag overrides this per run.

x-interview.ask: How should the story text appear on the pages? 'long' suits text-heavy books for ages 5-8 (~80+ words per spread).

text_background_prompt.description: Long mode only. Optional custom scene description for the book's shared text-page background (pages/text-bg-long.png — one model-generated image reused on every text page; the book style block is injected, no character references are sent, and a low-detail central area is reserved for text). Omit for a generic style-matched decorative background. Ignored in overlay/native modes.

language.description: Optional BCP-47 language tag for the book text (e.g. 'en', 'de', 'en-GB'). Used as dc:language metadata in EPUB output. Default: 'en'.

x-interview.ask: Book language (BCP-47 tag, e.g. en, de).

fonts.description: Optional book-wide map of text role -> font family name. Defines which font each per-page 'font' role uses. Values are family names (e.g. 'Arial', 'Patrick Hand') resolved at render time: bundled asset in assets/fonts/ -> system-installed font -> bundled role default. Omit to use the bundled Andika (reader) / PatrickHand (display).

x-interview.ask: Custom fonts for body text (reader) and titles (display); bundled Andika / Patrick Hand by default.

display.description: Title/cover font family. Default: Patrick Hand (bundled).

resolution.description: Optional book-wide image resolution for page rendering. 2K (default) is good for screen and print up to ~8×8 in; 1K is faster/cheaper for drafts; 4K for large-format print. The render CLI --resolution flag overrides this value when passed explicitly.

x-interview.ask: Render quality vs cost — 1K draft / 2K standard / 4K large-format print.

aspect_ratio.description: Optional book-wide aspect ratio applied to both style sheets and page renders. When omitted, the model picks framing on each call (non-deterministic). Set this to lock consistent framing across all sheets and pages (e.g. '4:3' for landscape, '3:4' for portrait, '1:1' for square). The stylesheet/render CLI --aspect-ratio flag overrides this value when passed explicitly.

x-interview.ask: Lock one page framing for the whole book, or leave unset to let the model choose per page.

saved_formats.description: Optional list of book file formats assembled after a full render: 'pdf' (multi-page PDF) and/or 'epub' (fixed-layout EPUB3). When omitted, ALL formats are produced. An empty array skips assembly. The render CLI --saved-formats flag overrides this value when passed explicitly ('none' to skip for one run).

x-interview.ask: Which finished book files to assemble after rendering.

cast.description: Names of the cast entries appearing on this page — characters, objects, and locations in ONE flat list, any mix and multiplicity (e.g. ['Pip', 'Red Umbrella', 'Gazelle Valley']). MUST match cast[].name exactly. Drives which reference images are sent when rendering this page. The FIRST entry whose kind is 'character' (or kind is absent, defaulting to character) is the page HERO — it additionally contributes its first ref_image photo for facial likeness; author the hero/child first among the characters. Objects and locations follow after characters. Use [] for scenery-only or subject-free pages.

text.description: Story text for this page/spread. Empty string for cover or wordless pages.

image_prompt.description: Full image generation prompt. Must name characters and mention style. Content only — do not include text-position or safe-zone directives; the render script appends those transparently from text_placement.

text_placement.description: Optional. Where text lands on the image. 'floating' (default, native mode only): the image model picks the most visually pleasing placement; the overlay path degrades this to 'bottom'. 'top'/'bottom': pin text to a fixed band. Unused on long-mode body pages (text goes to its own page); still honored for the long-mode cover.

text_color_hint.description: Optional hint for text color, e.g. 'dark' or 'light'. Default: dark.

text_align.description: Horizontal alignment of the overlay text. Default: left. Use 'center' for cover/title pages.

font.description: Font for the text overlay. 'reader' (Andika, body text) or 'display' (PatrickHand, titles/cover). Default: reader.

text_background_prompt.description: Long mode only. When set, this page's text page gets its OWN dedicated background (pages/page-NN-long-bg.png) generated from this description via ONE extra paid Gemini call, instead of the book's shared background (the book style block is injected; no character references are sent; a low-detail central area is reserved for text). Omit to use the shared book-wide background at no extra cost. Ignored in overlay/native modes and on the cover or empty-text pages. If set on an empty-text page a warning is logged and no text page is generated.
